messages.subject: Shading geom_line graph with geom_rects
parts:
I have a time series and I want to add vertical shading for the full height of the graph to show which range it is in. I use the rle and cumsum functions to calculate where the ranges start and end.  I then have to match those ranges to dates, which I do with the function trend.index - but I bet there is much better way to do this, yes?  

Also, the last thing I want to change about this - I want the color scheme to go from dark red to dark green (in scale_fill_manual), and for the labels to go in the same order as labels_, instead of alphabetical.  See the chart included here and it should make sense what I'm asking.

Thanks

require(xts)
require(ggplot2)

# create dummy data
set.seed(100)
trend <- 60 * sin(.05*1:100) + rnorm(mean = 0, sd = 10, 100)
cuts  <- c(-100, -50, -25, 25, 50, 100)
labels_  <- c('strong bear', 'bear', 'sideways', 'bull', 'strong bull')
dates <- seq(as.Date('2000-01-01'), len = 100, by = 'day')
df <- data.frame(dates, trend, market = cut(trend, cuts, labels_))

# number of consecutive values for market
runs <- rle(as.vector(df$market))
end_ <- cumsum(runs[['lengths']])
start_ <- c(0, end_[-length(end_)])

# get date of index 
trend.index <- function(index){
    if ( index == 0) x <- as.Date('20000101', '%Y%d%m')
    else x <- (df[index,]$dates)
    return(x)
}
date.start <- as.Date(sapply(start_, trend.index))
date.end <- as.Date(sapply(end_, trend.index))
market = runs[['values']]

# data for vertical rectangles 
runs.tla <- data.frame(date.start, date.end, market = market)
p  <- ggplot(df, aes(dates, trend)) + geom_line()
p <- p + geom_rect(aes(NULL, NULL, xmin = date.start, xmax = date.end, 
           fill = market), data = runs.tla, ymin = -100, ymax = 100) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(rainbow(5), 0.15))
p

parts:
Hi:

Try this, with a couple of bells and whistles added (theme_bw() to
brighten the colors a bit, size = 1 in geom_line() to thicken the time
series plot, use of expand = in scale_x_date to shrink the horizontal
margins).

set.seed(100)
trend <- 60 * sin(.05*1:100) + rnorm(mean = 0, sd = 10, 100)
cuts <- c(-100, -50, -25, 25, 50, 100)
labels_ <- c('strong bear', 'bear', 'sideways', 'bull', 'strong bull')
dates <- seq(as.Date('2000-01-01'), len = 100, by = 'day')
df <- data.frame(dates, trend, market = cut(trend, cuts, labels_))

df$market <- factor(df$market, levels = labels_)
## Defined in terms of
## 'bear', 'bull', 'sideways', 'strong bear', 'strong bull'
mycol <- c('green', 'red', 'goldenrod', 'darkgreen', 'darkred')

# number of consecutive values for market
runs <- rle(as.vector(df$market))
end_ <- cumsum(runs[['lengths']])
start_ <- c(0, end_[-length(end_)])

# get date of index
trend.index <- function(index){
if ( index == 0) x <- as.Date('20000101', '%Y%d%m')
else x <- (df[index,]$dates)
return(x)
}
date.start <- as.Date(sapply(start_, trend.index))
date.end <- as.Date(sapply(end_, trend.index))
market = runs[['values']]

# data for vertical rectangles
runs.tla <- data.frame(date.start, date.end, market = market)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(dates, trend)) + geom_line(size = 1) + theme_bw()

p <- p + geom_rect(aes(NULL, NULL, xmin = date.start, xmax = date.end,
fill = market), data = runs.tla, ymin = -100, ymax = 100)

p + scale_fill_manual(breaks = levels(df$market), values = alpha(mycol, 0.3)) +
scale_x_date(expand = c(0, 0.2))

For some reason, I had to define the colors in terms of the
lexicographical ordering of the market factor in df rather than in
terms of the (re)defined ordering. I would have expected the colors to
conform to the defined ordering, although I can guess what's going on.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Shading geom_line graph with geom_rects
parts:
Hi:

If someone knows how to get manual scales to accept hex codes, I'd
like to know. In the meantime, try this, which should be close. It
assumes the levels of df$market are ordered as in the legend of the
graph below.

set.seed(100)
trend <- 60 * sin(.05*1:100) + rnorm(mean = 0, sd = 10, 100)
cuts <- c(-100, -50, -25, 25, 50, 100)
labels_ <- c('strong bear', 'bear', 'sideways', 'bull', 'strong bull')
dates <- seq(as.Date('2000-01-01'), len = 100, by = 'day')
df <- data.frame(dates, trend,
market = ordered(cut(trend, cuts, labels_), levels = labels_))
df$market <- factor(df$market, levels = labels_)
runs <- rle(as.vector(df$market))

end_ <- cumsum(runs[['lengths']])
start_ <- c(0, end_[-length(end_)])

# get date of index
trend.index <- function(index){
if ( index == 0) x <- as.Date('20000101', '%Y%d%m')
else x <- (df[index,]$dates)
return(x)
}

date.start <- as.Date(sapply(start_, trend.index), origin = '1970-01-01')
date.end <- as.Date(sapply(end_, trend.index), origin = '1970-01-01')
market = runs[['values']]

# data for vertical rectangles
runs.tla <- data.frame(date.start, date.end, market = market)

# Substitute for the ColorBrewer RdYlGn palette
mycol <- c('red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'lightgreen', 'green')
# Reorder colors to lexicographic order of levels of df$market
# even though they're supposed to be ordered (!!)
mycol <- mycol[c(2, 4, 3, 1, 5)]

# Positioned geom_rect() before geom_line() -
# no transparency this time
p <- ggplot(df, aes(dates, trend)) +

geom_rect(aes(NULL, NULL, xmin = date.start, xmax = date.end,
fill = market), data = runs.tla, ymin = -100, ymax = 100) +

geom_line(size = 1) +
theme_bw() +
scale_x_date(expand = c(0, 0.2))
p + scale_fill_manual(breaks = levels(df$market), values = mycol)

The advantage of this approach is that you can use alpha transparency
on the color vector in scale_fill_manual. Had you been able to use the
Brewer palette with the proper matching of levels to colors (couldn't
do it myself), I don't know if you could have been able to apply
transparency since the palette = argument expects a character string
rather than an expression. In lieu of a better response, this should
hopefully be close to what you were after.

# Compare to
library('RColorBrewer')
p + scale_fill_brewer(pal = 'RdYlGn')
p + scale_fill_brewer(breaks = levels(df$market), pal = 'RdYlGn')

Dennis
